Jesus heals many and commands silence, with an Isaiah citation. **Context**: "The following passage is from **Matthew 16:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 28 verses and records Pharisees and Sadducees requesting a sign; Jesus refuses except the sign of Jonah and warns against their “leaven,” explained as their doctrine. In Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ; Jesus speaks of building his church, giving kingdom keys, and commands secrecy. Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection; rebukes Peter. He teaches self-denial, taking up the cross, final judgment, and some seeing the kingdom."

This chapter contains 35 verses and records Jesus healing a man’s withered hand in a synagogue on the sabbath, prompting Pharisees and Herodians to plot against him. It describes crowds from many regions seeking healing, unclean spirits calling him Son of God, and Jesus commanding silence. Jesus appoints the twelve apostles by name. His family seeks to restrain him, scribes accuse him of using Beelzebub, and he answers with sayings on division, binding the strong man, forgiveness and blasphemy against the Holy Ghost, and true kin as doers of God’s will."
**Verse**: "And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee."

verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Mark 5:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records Jesus crossing to the Gadarenes, casting unclean spirits (“Legion”) from a tomb-dwelling man into about two thousand swine, and being asked to depart; the healed man proclaims in Decapolis. Back across the sea, Jairus seeks healing for his dying daughter. A woman with a twelve-year issue of blood touches Jesus’ garment and is healed. Jesus raises Jairus’s twelve-year-old daughter and instructs secrecy and food."

This chapter contains 47 verses and records Jesus being delivered by the council to Pilate, questioned as King of the Jews, and accused while remaining mostly silent. Pilate releases Barabbas, scourges Jesus, and hands him to be crucified. Soldiers mock him; Simon of Cyrene carries the cross. Jesus is crucified at Golgotha with two thieves; darkness falls; he dies; the temple veil tears. A centurion comments; women watch. Joseph of Arimathea buries Jesus; Marys note the tomb."
**Verse**: "And straightway in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him to Pilate."

This chapter contains 35 verses and records Jesus teaching that disasters do not prove greater guilt and calling all to repent; he gives the parable of the barren fig tree. In a synagogue on the sabbath he heals a woman bowed eighteen years and answers the ruler. He compares God’s kingdom to mustard seed and leaven, teaches about the narrow gate and exclusion, notes people from all directions entering. Pharisees warn of Herod; Jesus speaks of his mission and laments Jerusalem’s rejection."
**Verse**: "And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in the kingdom of God."

verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Luke 14:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 35 verses and records Jesus dining at a chief Pharisee’s house on the Sabbath, healing a man with dropsy, and disputing Sabbath healing. He teaches a parable on taking the lowest seat and instructs hosts to invite the poor, maimed, lame, and blind. He gives the parable of the great supper with refused invitations and new guests gathered. He states conditions of discipleship, counting the cost, forsaking all, and warns about salt losing savor."

**Context**: "The following passage is from **Luke 18:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 43 verses and records Jesus’ parables of the persistent widow and the unjust judge, and the Pharisee and the publican praying in the temple. It describes Jesus blessing infants and teaching about receiving God’s kingdom like a child. A ruler asks about eternal life; Jesus cites commandments and tells him to sell possessions and follow him, teaching on riches and salvation. Jesus predicts his suffering, death, and resurrection, then heals a blind beggar near Jericho."

**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 3:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 36 verses and records Nicodemus, a Pharisee ruler, visiting Jesus at night and hearing about being born again, born of water and the Spirit, and the Son of man being lifted up for eternal life through belief. verses.text: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 9:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 41 verses and records Jesus healing a man blind from birth by making clay, anointing his eyes, and sending him to wash in the pool of Siloam on the Sabbath. Neighbors and Pharisees question the man and his parents; Pharisees dispute Jesus’ authority and expel the healed man. Jesus later identifies himself as the Son of God, and the man believes. Jesus speaks of spiritual sight and blindness to Pharisees."
**Verse**: "And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth."

verses.text: Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 11:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 57 verses and records Lazarus of Bethany becoming sick and dying, Jesus delaying, then traveling to Judea. Jesus meets Martha and Mary, speaks of resurrection and belief, weeps, and raises Lazarus from a cave tomb after four days. Many believe; others report to Pharisees. Chief priests and Pharisees, led by Caiaphas, plan Jesus’ death. Jesus withdraws to Ephraim as Passover approaches and leaders order his capture."
**Verse**: "Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha."

This chapter contains 26 verses and records Jesus praying to the Father to glorify him, affirming authority to give eternal life and defining it as knowing the true God and Jesus Christ. He prays for the disciples, not the world, asking their protection, joy, sanctification by truth, and unity. He notes one lost “son of perdition,” sends them into the world, and prays also for future believers to be one and share his glory and love."
**Verse**: "While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled."

verses.text: When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples.
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **John 18:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 40 verses and records Jesus crossing the brook Cedron to a garden, Judas leading officers to arrest him, and Peter cutting off Malchus’s ear before Jesus is bound and taken to Annas and then Caiaphas. Peter enters the courtyard and denies Jesus three times as the cock crows. Jesus is questioned about his teaching and struck. Jesus is brought to Pilate, speaks of his kingship and truth, and Pilate finds no fault; the crowd chooses Barabbas for release."
**Verse**: "When Jesus had spoken these words, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where was a garden, into the which he entered, and his disciples."

This chapter contains 25 verses and records Jesus appearing to disciples at the Sea of Tiberias, directing a catch of 153 fish and eating with them. **Context**: "The following passage is from **Acts 18:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 28 verses and records Paul’s ministry in Corinth with Aquila and Priscilla, his synagogue reasoning, and many Corinthians believing and being baptized, including Crispus. verses.text: Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.

**Context**: "The following passage is from **Romans 10:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records Paul’s prayer for Israel’s salvation and his claim that Israel seeks its own righteousness rather than God’s. verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Corinthians 5:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records Paul addressing reported sexual immorality in the Corinthian church, specifically a man having his father’s wife. He rebukes their pride and instructs them, when assembled in Jesus’ name, to remove the offender and deliver him to Satan for destruction of the flesh. He uses leaven imagery to command purging wickedness, and directs believers not to associate or eat with professing brothers who practice specified sins, while distinguishing judgment inside the church from outsiders."
**Verse**: "It is reported commonly that there is fornication among you, and such fornication as is not so much as named among the Gentiles, that one should have his father's wife."

verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Corinthians 13:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 13 verses and covers Paul’s teaching that spiritual gifts, knowledge, faith, sacrifice, and martyrdom are worthless without charity. It lists charity’s qualities: patience, kindness, humility, selflessness, restraint, truthfulness, endurance, and hope. It contrasts charity’s permanence with the passing of prophecies, tongues, and knowledge, notes present partial understanding versus future completeness, and states faith, hope, and charity remain, with charity greatest."
**Verse**: "Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal."

This chapter contains 24 verses and records Paul’s instructions for a collection for the saints, weekly setting aside funds, and sending approved messengers to Jerusalem. It covers his travel plans through Macedonia, possible wintering in Corinth, and remaining at Ephesus until Pentecost. Paul gives directions about Timothy and Apollos, exhorts steadfastness and charity, commends Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, sends greetings, and adds a warning and closing benediction."
**Verse**: "As touching our brother Apollos, I greatly desired him to come unto you with the brethren: but his will was not at all to come at this time; but he will come when he shall have convenient time."

**Context**: "The following passage is from **Philippians 1:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 30 verses and records Paul and Timothy greeting the saints at Philippi, including bishops and deacons, and giving thanks and prayer for their fellowship and growth in love and righteousness. verses.text: Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Thessalonians 1:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 10 verses and records Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy greeting the Thessalonian church with grace and peace, giving thanks and praying for their faith, love, and hope. It notes the gospel coming with power and assurance, and the believers receiving the word amid affliction with joy. The church becomes an example in Macedonia and Achaia, spreads the message, turns from idols to serve God, and waits for God’s Son from heaven, raised from the dead."
**Verse**: "Paul, and Silvanus, and Timotheus, unto the church of the Thessalonians which is in God the Father and in the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace be unto you, and peace, from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ."

verses.text: For yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Thessalonians 2:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records Paul’s defense of his ministry in Thessalonica: he preaches boldly after suffering at Philippi, speaks without deceit or flattery, and works to avoid burdening them. He describes gentle, parental care, exhorts them to walk worthy of God, and thanks God for their reception of the word. He notes their persecutions, his desire to revisit, Satan’s hindrance, and their joy at Christ’s coming."
**Verse**: "For yourselves, brethren, know our entrance in unto you, that it was not in vain:"

verses.text: But even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully entreated, as ye know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God with much contention.

verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Thessalonians 3:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records Paul’s request for prayer for the spread of the word and deliverance from wicked men, affirming the Lord’s faithfulness. He commands believers to withdraw from disorderly brethren, cites his own labor as an example, and orders that unwilling workers not eat. He instructs busybodies to work quietly, urges perseverance in doing good, directs discipline without treating offenders as enemies, and closes with peace, a signed greeting, and a benediction."

**Context**: "The following passage is from **1 Timothy 1:1** from the **New Testament**. verses.text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Hebrews 12:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 29 verses and describes exhortations to run the race by laying aside sin and looking to Jesus who endured the cross. It explains God’s chastening of sons and urges endurance, straight paths, peace, and holiness, avoiding bitterness and immorality like Esau. It contrasts Sinai’s fearsome scene with heavenly Zion, the new covenant, and Jesus’ sprinkled blood, warning not to refuse God’s voice and noting a final shaking and an unshakable kingdom."
**Verse**: "Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,"

This chapter contains 22 verses and warns of false teachers who introduce heresies, exploit others, and face certain judgment. It cites past examples: sinful angels cast into chains, the flood with Noah preserved, and Sodom and Gomorrah destroyed while Lot is delivered. verses.text: This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you; in both which I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance:
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **2 Peter 3:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 18 verses and records Peter’s second letter urging remembrance of prophets and apostolic commands, warning that scoffers question the Lord’s coming. It cites creation and the flood, and states the present heavens and earth are reserved for fire at judgment. It explains the Lord’s timing and patience, describes the day of the Lord’s sudden arrival and cosmic dissolution, anticipates new heavens and a new earth, exhorts holiness, references Paul’s letters, warns against distortion and error, and commands growth in grace and knowledge of Jesus Christ."
**Verse**: "This second epistle, beloved, I now write unto you; in both which I stir up your pure minds by way of remembrance:"

verses.text: Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called:
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Jude 1:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 25 verses and records Jude’s greeting and blessing, an exhortation to contend for the faith, and a warning about ungodly intruders who deny the Lord and corrupt conduct. It recalls judgments on unbelieving Israel, rebellious angels, and Sodom and Gomorrah, and cites Michael’s dispute with the devil. It compares the deceivers to Cain, Balaam, and Korah, quotes Enoch on coming judgment, urges believers to build faith, pray, show mercy, and ends with a doxology."
**Verse**: "Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to them that are sanctified by God the Father, and preserved in Jesus Christ, and called:"

This chapter contains 25 verses and records Jude’s greeting and blessing, an exhortation to contend for the faith, and a warning about ungodly intruders who deny the Lord and corrupt conduct. It recalls judgments on unbelieving Israel, rebellious angels, and Sodom and Gomorrah, and cites Michael’s dispute with the devil. It compares the deceivers to Cain, Balaam, and Korah, quotes Enoch on coming judgment, urges believers to build faith, pray, show mercy, and ends with a doxology."
**Verse**: "Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever."

verses.text: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John:
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Revelation 1:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 20 verses and records John introducing the revelation given by God through an angel, blessing readers who keep it, and addressing seven churches in Asia. From Patmos John hears a trumpet-like voice commanding him to write to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea. He sees seven candlesticks and the Son of man holding seven stars, declares his authority over death, and explains stars and candlesticks."
**Verse**: "The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John:"

This chapter contains 29 verses and records messages to the churches in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, and Thyatira. It notes each church’s works and challenges, calls for repentance or faithfulness, warns of judgment (removing a candlestick, prison, fighting with the sword, tribulation), mentions Nicolaitans, Balaam, Antipas, and “Jezebel,” and promises rewards to overcomers (tree of life, crown of life, hidden manna, white stone, authority over nations, morning star)."

**Context**: "The following passage is from **Revelation 5:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 17 verses and records John seeing four angels restraining the earth’s winds, and another angel commanding no harm until God’s servants are sealed. It lists 144,000 sealed from twelve tribes of Israel. John then sees an innumerable multitude from all nations before the throne and the Lamb, worshiping. An elder identifies them as coming from great tribulation, serving in God’s temple, sheltered from hunger and heat, led by the Lamb."
**Verse**: "For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes."

verses.text: And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour.
verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Revelation 8:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 13 verses and records the opening of the seventh seal and a half-hour silence in heaven. Seven angels receive trumpets, and another angel offers incense with the prayers of the saints, then casts fire to earth causing thunder, lightning, and an earthquake. The first four trumpets bring hail and fire with blood, a burning mountain in the sea, the star Wormwood poisoning waters, and darkness on sun, moon, and stars. An angel announces three coming woes."
**Verse**: "And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven about the space of half an hour."

verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Revelation 9:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 21 verses and records the fifth and sixth trumpet judgments. A star receives the key to the bottomless pit, releasing smoke and locusts that torment unsealed people for five months under Abaddon/Apollyon. Then four angels bound at the Euphrates are loosed to kill a third of humanity by an immense cavalry with fire, smoke, and brimstone. Survivors do not repent of idolatry, murders, sorceries, fornication, or thefts."
**Verse**: "And the fifth angel sounded, and I saw a star fall from heaven unto the earth: and to him was given the key of the bottomless pit."

verses.context:
**Context**: "The following passage is from **Revelation 10:1** from the **New Testament**. This chapter contains 11 verses and records John seeing a mighty angel descend from heaven with an open little book, standing on sea and earth and crying out as seven thunders speak. John is commanded to seal up the thunders’ words. The angel swears by the Creator that time is no longer and that God’s mystery is finished when the seventh angel sounds. This chapter contains 17 verses and records signs in heaven of a woman clothed with the sun who bears a male child, and a red dragon seeking to devour him. The child is caught up to God, and the woman flees to the wilderness for 1,260 days. War occurs in heaven as Michael casts Satan and his angels to earth. A heavenly voice announces the accuser’s defeat. The dragon persecutes the woman, sends a flood, the earth swallows it, and he makes war on her remnant who keep God’s commandments and hold Jesus’ testimony."
**Verse**: "And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon; and the dragon fought and his angels,"

God names himself Alpha and Omega, promises the water of life and inheritance to overcomers, and assigns the wicked to the lake of fire. An angel shows and measures the city’s gates, foundations, materials, light, open gates, and exclusion of the defiled."
**Verse**: "And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb's book of life."

verses.text: And he shewed me a pure river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb.
